title: Gaila, the Laughing Light
subtitle: The Joke Shared at the Wrong Time

lore.description:
Gaila is recognized at the instant two people try not to laugh and fail together. A quarrel pauses over a foolish song; someone makes room at the table to hear the rest of a joke. Her followers tend these small openings. They keep games children can teach strangers and know which friend needs company without being asked to speak. The Laughing Light's gifts make joy easier to share. Her most devoted servants struggle when the room grows quiet and nobody wants cheering up.

**A daughter who will not keep everyone at home.**

Gaila belongs to Inaea's daughters, but the family resemblance has limits. A shared joke can open a connection that no one intends to preserve. Grandmothers who invoke the Weaver may welcome her daughter's interruption and then complain when the guest leaves without promising to return. Gaila's household stories favor the person who makes room for delight without deciding beforehand what relationship it must produce.

Among Aelaerem, her small observances live inside a welcome that is already sincere. A child is allowed to teach a visitor a game badly; the adults refrain from correcting the rules until the visitor has won once. Some households preserve versions so different that cousins have to learn again when they visit. The pleasure is in playing together, and not a hidden admission price to the household.

**The traveling fool and the borrowed game.**

The Gigglemoon name spread with performers who could teach a game across a language boundary more quickly than they could explain a play. It sounds childish to some of their descendants, who now manage theaters or entertain courts. Older companies keep it on the box of ordinary props that an apprentice is permitted to borrow without asking.

In Thepyrgos, working companies invoke the Laughing Light before the rehearsal at which servants and scenery hands may interrupt the lead performer. The custom began as a way to test whether a joke reached beyond its author. Wealthy patrons later hired it as an evening's entertainment, paying for the appearance of being corrected. Performers argue about whether a lord who chooses the subject has allowed himself to be laughed at at all.

At Nihori spring gatherings, some shrine households invite an out-of-season fool to perform only after the formal observance has closed. This local accommodation lets neighbors enjoy an interruption without treating every interruption as properly made. It has also produced an unpopular office: the attendant who must tell a successful performer that the allowed interval is over.

**Joy after the work.**

In Ngomebe, crews have adapted the traveling games for streets that will not remain level. A dropped counter can decide a round, and an Aeler engineer who insists on measuring the board becomes part of the amusement. Such evenings spread between cities with repair crews and marriages. They create friendships beyond the House assigning a shift, which is why some elders sponsor them and others want attendance announced in advance.

Gaila's attendants are divided over celebrations after a death. One company returns every year because a bereaved household once laughed at its performance. Another waits to be invited, even when the absence costs its members work. Neither has lost devotion by recognizing grief. The dangerous turn comes when a successful keeper begins treating a quiet room as a failure that must be corrected. A festival patron who requires every household to send someone can make that disagreement public; the question is whether joy still welcomes anyone when it stops permitting an empty seat.
lore.followers: Her followers learn that the strongest bond is forged not in sorrow, but in laughter; not in sacrifice, but in shared delight. To serve her is to become a spark: someone who turns ordinary moments into games, who sees the humor in stumbles, and who understands that a smile given freely is a gift that asks for nothing in return. In the taverns where strangers become friends over foolish songs, in palace gardens where princes and paupers trade riddles, in quiet kitchens where couples dance while burning dinner, Gaila's influence is felt. Her cults are the Gigglemoon, whose members seal joy with shared bubbles and silly vows. Her witches are jesters who brew teas that induce giggles, toymakers who craft puzzles requiring two hands to solve, and bakers who hide fortunes in cookies.
lore.quote: The truest vow is not spoken — it is laughed. When joy flows between you like water, you need no chains; your bond is the laughter that keeps you afloat.

domain_focus: Playful Intimacy: shared laughter, inside jokes, the joy of simple companionship
Lighthearted Bonding: oaths of mirth, playful teasing as affection, the magic of mundane happiness
Rituals of Delight: games, shared silliness, spontaneous merriment, the sacred ordinary
Healing Through Joy: dissolving tension with humor, restoring lightness after sorrow, communal buoyancy

thiasos.description: Gaila's Thiasos is a small being of joy: a pair of butterflies that dance in sync only when two people laugh together, a songbird that trills a silly tune when tickled near a smiling face, a fox kit that playfully steals small tokens from friends' pockets, or a dandelion clock whose seeds float only when blown by two laughing breaths.
thiasos.care: Beyond its ordinary care, this Thiasos must be given a token of shared joy each day (a recalled laugh shared aloud, a doodle exchanged that makes both grin, a pebble from a place where joy was felt). If that need goes unmet, the Thiasos becomes Compromised: its aura of lightness turns brittle, imposing –1 die on all Sway rolls involving genuine mirth for its bearer until offered a fresh token of mutual delight.

codex.description: One will not find Gaila's Codex written as a book of dry ink. It may be a journal whose pages fill with doodles and jokes when laughter touches it, a set of three bells that chime in harmony only when two people smile at once, a deck of cards where each pair bears a private joke only the holders understand, or a hollow gourd that rattles with joyous noise when shaken by happy hands.
codex.upkeep: Because Gaila's truths are written in shared merriment, the Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week engaged in a ritual of pure joy with another (playing a childish game until both laugh until tears, sharing three silly memories that spark giggles, or simply sitting in silence while exchanging smiles that reach the eyes), or the Rites stored there fade (treat as Compromised until re-joyed).

patrons_gift.name: Gaila's Spark
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of Gaila may touch a held item (weapon, tool, or garment) and breathe a single word of "laugh."
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Sway or Performance rolls, and the first time each scene the bearer shares a moment of genuine joy with a target they wish to charm (a shared laugh, a silly exchange, mutual delight in simplicity), the target must test Resolve (DV 3) or feel a wave of lighthearted warmth (suffer –1 die to resist the bearer's next social action).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to Gaila.

rites.name: Rite of the Shared Chuckle
rites.materials: A silly joke told in confidence, or a token meant to provoke a smile (a funny pebble, a joke-novelty).
rites.effect: Your mirth becomes contagious. Gain +1 die to Sway one target in a joyful exchange. The target feels a subtle lift of spirit; they are more likely to remember your presence fondly.
rites.push_it: The target feels safe enough to name a hidden delight (a secret pleasure, a guilty joy). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Inside Joke
rites.materials: Two matching silly trinkets (e.g., mismatched socks, novelty buttons), or a shared doodle only the pair understands.
rites.effect: Create a temporary bond of playful kinship. Both parties gain +1 die when aiding each other in acts of lighthearted teasing or shared amusement. The bond manifests as a shared warmth, like sunlight on skin after laughter.
rites.push_it: The bond deepens to shared vulnerability; both sense when the other is hiding joy but suffer –1 die to conceal their own delight. The bond may persist as a gentle ache until the next dusk. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of Endless Mirth
rites.materials: Perfume applied while recalling a joyful memory, or a garment worn that feels like a second skin of happiness.
rites.effect: Assume an aura of effortless charm and magnetic lightness. Gain +2 dice to Sway or Performance in settings of playfulness or shared delight. Your presence lingers in the memory like a half-remembered giggle.
rites.push_it: Become the embodiment of joy; all who interact with you feel a shiver of "more, please" (Resolve DV 2 to resist seeking deeper connection). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Joy's Embrace
rites.materials: Token exchanged as a promise of joy — a shared silly vow spoken into wind, a length of ribbon tied in a bow then loosened, or a stone warmed by mutual grip during laughter.
rites.effect: Forge a promise of mutual delight. Both gain +1 Effect when cooperating in acts of shared playfulness or lighthearted bonding; breach inflicts 1 SB (Hearts) and a hollowness where laughter once was. Create a 6-segment Joy Strength timer.
rites.push_it: Breach also causes a visible withdrawal (a tendency to deflect humor, a habit of taking things too seriously, or an inability to linger in lighthearted space). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Gigglemoon Circle
rites.materials: A circle of stones, each touched by a participant's tear of laughter; a chalice filled with sparkling cider shared sip by sip; a length of silk woven from threads spun in mutual silliness.
rites.effect: You become the heart of a joyful zone. For the scene: you gain +1 Effect on all social rolls focused on playfulness or mutual delight, and opponents suffer –1 die when attempting to impose seriousness or demand solemnity. Anyone who attempts to deceive you about their emotional state must test Resolve (DV 4) or reveal a hidden sorrow. Allies who share a ritual of pure joy regain 1 Fatigue. Start a 10-segment Circle of Giggles timer; when it fills, you may declare one irrevocable social judgment that the zone's inhabitants will uphold for one month.
rites.push_it: Newcomers must test Resolve (DV 4) or become briefly inclined toward joy — they will accept one simple act of mutual delight. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of Gaila sings in harmonies of mirth — melodies that linger like the echo of a shared laugh, the hum of a tune only two know. Their voice is used to spark a friendship that lasts a lifetime, to seal a pact of mutual playfulness with a hum, or to draw out the unspoken joy in a guarded heart. Gaila's Cantors are sought in festivals and taverns, and valued by those who know that true joy needs no grand gesture — only the courage to be delightfully present.

cult.name: The Cult of the Gigglemoon
cult.description: Gaila's cults are not hidden; they meet in sunlit meadows, taverns at dusk, and porch swings where the talk turns silly. The Gigglemoon appears to be a society of joy-seekers — but its members trade in time, attention, and the gift of being seen as delightful. A ritual involves each member blowing a bubble shared with another while naming a joy they wish to nurture. The bubble solution is mixed from a common source; those who share a bubble become bound to the Circle — they cannot dismiss a member's bid for play without suffering a visible flush (1 Fatigue, no roll). Their creed is embroidered on its seal: "Every laugh shared is a thread lightened. Every thread lightened makes the joy unbreakable."

witchcraft.name: The Art of the Glee-Weaver
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with Gaila is a glee-weaver or joy-smith — one who crafts social reality from threads of shared silliness, spontaneous merriment, and the courage to play. Their magic works with the tools of delight: a powder that induces gentle giggles, a toy that requires two hands to operate (forcing cooperation), or a charm that makes mundane tasks feel like games. Their tools are never solemn; they use fans, noisemakers, and the subtle art of the well-timed "let's pretend."
witchcraft.lore: In Ecktoria, a Gaila witch might be a letter-writer for the lonely, sealing each envelope with a pressed flower from a shared walk of laughter. In Aeler, a True-Mason might carve a bench that makes every shared silence upon it carry the echo of mutual chuckling. Glee-weavers rarely see their craft as magic at all — they call it kindness with better tools.
witchcraft.quote: Every laugh shared is a thread lightened.

giggle_dust.name: Giggle Dust
giggle_dust.description: A pinch of shimmering powder that grows warm when two people share a genuine laugh. Once per session, the witch may blow a single pinch while focusing on a person they have met. That dust becomes a token of shared joy — when present between that person and another, it grants +1 die to resist despair or hopelessness (GM determines effect). The witch cannot control how the token is used, only that it exists — and that a token born of shared mirth is the hardest to ignore.

hedge_gifts.name: Joy's Touch
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may touch a person's hand (or a letter they have written) and speak a single word of intent ("play," "laugh," "delight"). For the next hour, the target feels a mild but genuine inclination toward that emotion or action, granting the wielder +1 die on social rolls against them when engaging in playful teasing.

hedge_gifts.name: Pocket Fool
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, you may craft an instant improvised toy or trick from mundane materials at hand (a coin, a napkin, a stick). Anyone who plays with it for a moment gains a temporary +1 die to their next social roll made in good humor.

hedge_gifts.name: Sugar in the Tea
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, when tension threatens to boil over into violence or despair, you may spend an action to defuse it with a well-timed jest. All parties gain +1 die to any roll made to de-escalate the situation this scene.

hedge_gifts.name: The Well-Timed Wink
hedge_gifts.description: Passive. Once per scene, you may reroll a failed Sway or Performance roll if the attempt involved humor, teasing, or playful charm.

monastic_tradition.name: The Way of the Open Hand
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Open Hand train not in stillness but in play — sparring matches that dissolve into laughter, forms practiced as games, meditation broken deliberately by a well-timed joke. They believe that the body carries its burdens in tension, and that tension yields fastest to delight. Their monasteries ring with sound most orders would call undisciplined: children's games repurposed as combat drills, festival songs sung during work, mock trials held for the crime of frowning too long.
monastic_tradition.quote: The truest vow is not spoken — it is laughed.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Presence 3+, Spirit 2+, Rite of the Shared Chuckle or Cantor of Gaila.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: A debt held lightly is easier to set down. Monks of the Open Hand gain +1 die to resist any magical debt, geas, or contract sealed under duress, sorrow, or coercion (once per scene). If they succeed, they answer the compulsion with laughter, and the binding finds no purchase in a heart too light to hold it.

basic.name: Disarming Grin
basic.description: Once per scene, in place of an attack, you may offer a target a genuine moment of levity. They must test Resolve (DV 3) or lose their next action to a startled laugh (they are not harmed, merely delighted).

advanced.name: Contagious Delight
advanced.description: Once per scene, all allies within Near who share a moment of genuine laughter with you clear 1 Fatigue and gain +1 die to their next social roll.

master.name: The Unbreakable Smile
master.description: Once per session, you may declare that no harm within Near range this scene may break the joy of a gathering — Fear and Despair effects are resisted at +2 dice by all present. After the scene, you gain a permanent Debt Scar (a laugh line that never fades, visible even in grief) but +1 die to resist your own despair for the rest of the session.

monastic_tradition.corruption_note: Monks follow the patron's general Corruption track; the monastic path does not add a second one. Where a tradition needs its own, it must differ from the general track in kind, not degree.

corruption.benefit: Glee's Touch: +1 die to Sway or Performance when playful or joyful.
corruption.cost: Need for Mirth: –1 die when acting without lightheartedness or delight.

corruption.benefit: Heart's Lightness: Once/scene, +2 dice to sense hidden joys or unspoken pleasures.
corruption.cost: Emotional Whiplash: Mark 1 Fatigue if unable to sustain joy or mutual delight.

corruption.benefit: Aura of Buoyancy: Allies in Near gain +1 die to resist despair or hopelessness.
corruption.cost: Pleasure Magnet: Others sense your allure and lean into fantasy, often seeking escape through you.

corruption.benefit: Veil of Delight: Once/session, issue a compelling invitation to "play" that feels like a shared dream (Resist DV 4).
corruption.cost: Fear of Seriousness: –1 die to engage in solemn matters, especially when joy is sweet.

corruption.benefit: Joy Keeper: Once/session, call on contacts for aid — they remember the thrill of your shared laugh.
corruption.cost: Hollow Delight: –1 die when isolated from those you play with; you hunger for the thrill of the lighthearted.

corruption.benefit: Sovereign Merriment: Once/session, dominate a gathering in joy; all who meet your eyes must test Resolve (DV 5) or feel compelled to seek your lightness.
corruption.cost: The Eternal Giggle: Mark +2 Obligation; your presence becomes a tease when you cannot delight, and you cannot stop chasing the shimmer just out of reach.

playstyle_notes.description: Gaila's gifts turn play into an opening: strangers cooperate over a game, or a shared joke lets a frightened companion speak. Her corruption makes quiet company harder to bear. Give the follower occasions when the kindest response is to let someone be sad, even when they could make the room laugh. Use Lines & Veils for scenes involving vulnerability.

Lighthearted Bonding: oaths of mirth, playful teasing as affection, the magic of mundane happiness
The Pleasure of Simple Being: finding joy in ordinary moments, shared delight in simplicity
Healing Through Joy: dissolving tension with humor, restoring lightness after sorrow

sample_adventure.title: The Gigglemoon's Debt
sample_adventure.description: A beloved local jester — a devotee of the Gigglemoon — has stopped laughing, and the whole town has noticed the difference in ways they cannot quite name: shorter tempers, colder greetings, a market square gone quiet. The party learns the jester owes the Circle a joy they can no longer supply, and must find a way to restore what was lost before the Gigglemoon calls the debt due in a far crueler currency than laughter.
sample_adventure.quote: We do not ask for gold. We ask only that you remember how to laugh — and that, sometimes, is the harder debt to pay.

lineage: A daughter of Inaea — born of the Spider's line, spinning beyond the web's architecture.

guises.name: The Second Laugh
guises.note: A wooden spoon with a face cut into its handle is handed to whoever must begin the evening's game. The carving is usually very poor. Children learn that the second person to laugh has done something important: they have made the first person's foolishness companionable. A guest may pass the spoon without performing. Some Gigglemoon circles have forgotten that courtesy and remember only the game.

guises.among: Thepyrgos's gardens and small performance houses
guises.name: Elyra of the Open Hand
guises.note: Her image offers a little clay bird rather than a cup. Garden dedications sometimes place her among attendant graces, although learned catalogues give her a name of her own. Vendors sell inexpensive birds beside the polished ones commissioned by patrons. The clumsy whistle made by a cheap bird can interrupt a distinguished speaker more effectively than an actor's prepared joke.

guises.name: The Unbraided Moment
guises.note: After the serious naming at the oak-ring, a singer deliberately gives the host an absurd additional title. The host must supply a better one for the singer. A successful exchange lets guests answer without first establishing rank. The custom has limits everyone pretends to know until an outsider crosses one; then the host's response reveals how much of the evening's welcome was real.

guises.name: The Laugh on the Return Boat
guises.note: An overturned toy boat is set beside the shrine after a frightened crew comes home. Children right it during the next household game. The observance makes room for the foolish thing someone said while afraid, without requiring them to describe the danger. Ferry entertainers carried Gigglemoon games ashore; local families shortened them to fit the interval before the next departure.

provenance.origin: Gaila is one of Inaea's four daughters. Her cult remembers countless first shared laughs without making each one an alternative divine birth.
provenance.summary: Household tokens seldom survive with the names of their makers. A spoon is used until its face wears away; a whistle is broken; the words of a game change when a child misunderstands them. Thepyrgos's collectors began preserving such objects as evidence of an older graceful company. Their arrangements made Elyra respectable enough for a garden sanctuary, but sometimes removed the very mistakes that had made a family keep the object.
provenance.the_migration: Nurses, married-in relatives, traveling players, and children returning from fosterage spread observances more readily than formal missionaries. A game might cross a border before its divine name did. A later Cantor could recognize its turn-taking, add Gaila's invocation, and be told that the grandmother who taught it had never needed that verse. Some communities accepted the name while continuing to credit the grandmother.
provenance.why_it_took: The Gigglemoon offers something people seek for its own sake. Companionship can grow around an undignified song when a formal reconciliation has failed. Its larger circles acquired patrons who expected a reliably happy feast. Paid celebrants then faced a different obligation: somebody had promised the host that the guests would enjoy themselves. The move from shared play to commissioned delight produced the Laughing Light's most persistent quarrels.
provenance.note: Gaila's followers can recognize Thrysos's dancers and Palinode's singers as welcome company without treating their gatherings as the same observance. Her small pleasure can survive an imperfect song or an early departure. Her more devoted celebrants find both increasingly difficult to allow. The moment when a tired friend asks them to stop may trouble them more than an insult.

philosophy.name: A Joy That Can Be Declined
philosophy.summary: Gaila's gift begins when delight passes between people. The host cannot establish that it was shared simply by making everyone smile.
philosophy.the_point: An old joke can carry years of affection. It can also preserve the role assigned to a person who no longer enjoys playing it. A circle may miss their old companion sincerely while refusing to meet the one sitting before them.
philosophy.the_third_thing: There are observances in which the spoon is passed around twice. On the second circuit, anyone may put it down. The most skillful celebrants make that ending feel as welcome as the first laugh.
philosophy.at_the_table: A town asks its former jester to resume a festival that once brought rival households together. The jester wants to help, but the piece everybody requests depends on humiliating someone now old enough to object. Give the replacement performance room to be genuinely funny; the answer need not be to abolish the feast or compel its old target to forgive.
